About memery

Serious experience.
A good story to tell.

We’re strategists, writers, producers and people who ask one more question. We help organisations understand their audiences, use AI intelligently and make content people choose to spend time with.

Good strategy.
Great stories.
Actual humans.

memery brings together the science of being remembered and the craft of making something worth remembering. That means audience insights with a purpose, practical AI that helps teams do better work, and stories built for the places people actually watch, read and listen.

At the heart of it are Matt and Riley: a former journalist turned marketing leader, and a radio all-rounder turned podcast host and producer. Between them, they can find the angle, build the strategy, write the script and get it on air. They can also talk for quite a while. Fortunately, knowing what to leave out is part of the job.

The people behind memery

Meet Matt and Riley.

Matt Granfield

Founder, writer, marketer, recovering hipster.

Matt has spent more than 20 years finding the story, building the audience and giving people a reason to care. His career began in journalism, with a News Limited cadetship and writing for the ABC, Crikey, The Courier-Mail and Marketing Magazine.

His communications degree took him into music and audio production, and an internship at triple j gave him an early education in content, culture and the art of getting people to listen. Then he wrote an entire book about hipsters. Published by Allen & Unwin, HipsterMattic became a bestseller. Yes, he has heard the jokes. Some of them are in the book.

Somewhere along the way, Matt added strategy to the storytelling. He studied Strategic Marketing Management at Harvard Business School, completed an MBA at UQ and held senior marketing and digital roles at Heritage Bank, Mantra Group, Brisbane’s economic development agency and Economic Development Queensland. As Chief Marketing Officer and Executive Director of Customer Experience at Charles Sturt University, he led a team of more than 100 people. At Mantra, he built a loyalty program with more than a million members. He understands the creative idea and the business case it needs to answer.

He’s also the founder of Spare Keys, a tech-for-good charity that connects unused resources with people who need technology and crisis accommodation. It has helped more than 1,000 people — proof that a useful idea can do considerably more than win a meeting.

Riley-Rose Harper

Producer, presenter, writer, professional maker-of-good-stuff.

Riley has spent the best part of a decade figuring out how to make people stop, listen and actually care. She cut her teeth at Southern Cross Austereo, spending more than seven years doing pretty much everything you can do near a microphone: promotions, announcing, producing and creating digital content.

Radio taught her how to find an angle, keep a conversation moving and make something interesting before the next ad break. It also taught her to keep talking when the technology stops working — a surprisingly transferable skill.

She’s since taken those instincts into podcasting as host and producer of How To Turn 30, and through her work on Charles Sturt University’s The Uni Years and Charles Sturt Parent Podcast. From the first idea to the final edit, she knows how to turn a subject into a conversation people want to hear.

She’s also a freelance writer whose work has appeared in Mamamia, 9Honey and The Border Mail. Whether it’s a podcast, an article or a piece of digital content, Riley brings an ear for the good bit and a healthy impatience with the boring bit.

Let’s make something worth remembering.

Got a story to tell, an audience to understand or a marketing team ready to put AI to work? We’d love to hear about it.
